title: BUILDING THE - ABANDONED IDE
author: Santhosh
shortDescription: A journey through building a lightweight Flutter-based IDE for Windows.

data.content: The idea behind THE - ABANDONED IDE started with a simple question: what if an IDE could understand the project instead of simply displaying files and running commands?
I wanted to experiment with building a lightweight desktop development environment using Flutter and Dart while keeping the interface focused entirely on the developer.
The first version was intentionally simple. I started with the project explorer, file creation, file editing, and a built-in terminal.

Getting the filesystem interaction working correctly was one of the first interesting challenges. The IDE needed to understand folders, nested files, newly created files, and changes made outside the application.
Once those fundamentals were working, the editor started feeling like an actual development environment rather than just another Flutter interface.

The next stage is where the project becomes much more interesting. Instead of treating AI as a simple chatbot, I want it to understand the structure of the project and work with the developer's files and tools.
The goal is to eventually connect the IDE with an AI agent capable of analysing project files, understanding dependencies, generating code, and interacting with the development environment.
This is still an evolving experiment, but the foundation is now in place to build something much more ambitious.

dyks.title: Flutter can target Windows
dyks.description: Flutter is not limited to mobile applications. It can also be used to build native Windows desktop applications.

dyks.title: Dart is the language behind Flutter
dyks.description: Flutter applications are primarily written using Dart, which provides the language features used to build Flutter interfaces and application logic.
